To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

composite films of poly (vinyl alcohol)-chito-san-bacterial cellulose can be prepared to achieve controlled re-lease of drugs, with a good agreement to the Fickian diffusion model, and with a release rate decreasing as the BC concentration is increased.

composite films of PVA/chitosan/bacterial cellulose can be prepared by simple and low cost methods, the films are suitable for controlled release of Ibu Na as drug, and the release of IbuNA can be controlled by the composition of the film and the pH of the release media.
the PVA/chitosan composite films containing BC as filler are promising candidates for controlled release of drugs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of composite films based on BC, PVA and chitosan that can be applied in drug controlled release systems.
the development of a novel system based on composite films with a controlled release capacity of IbuNa.

the design of composite films of PVA/chitosan/bacterial cellulose (BC) for the controlled delivery of ibuprofen, a nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug, in two different pH media, pH 1.5 and pH 7, which mimic the gastrointestinal tract conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PVA/chitosan composite films containing BC can be successfully used as a controlled release drug carrier.
the PVA/chitosan/bacterial cellulose composite films have a potential for controlled drug release applications.
the composite films are suitable as drug carriers for oral drug delivery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the composite films of PVA/chitosan and BC are promising for controlled release of IbuNA.
composite films of PVA-chitosan-BC are promising systems for controlled release of drugs.
PVA-chitosan-BC films can be considered as a promising drug delivery system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
composite films with different BC content can be used for controlled release of active substances.
the composite films of PVA/chitosan-BC can be used as a promising drug carrier for controlled release of IbuNA in the gastrointestinal tract.
composite films of PVA, chitosan and BC can be used for controlled drug release.
